title: gdacs-tc-1001305's second life will never be resolved -- resolve_pending's one-resolution-per-id guard means a future's REAPPEARED episode has no path to ever getting measured
statement: foreknown/registry.json's futures['gdacs-tc-1001305'] shows a full life-death-life cycle: NOTARIZED 2026-08-22T05:58:52+00:00, REVISED twice (2026-08-23, 2026-08-24, the second adding China to `where`), CLOSED_BY_SOURCE 2026-08-25T06:04:45+00:00, then REAPPEARED 2026-08-28T17:41:45+00:00 (snapshot foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-28/gdacs.json) with a same-timestamp REVISED extending the window to 2026-08-28 and reordering `where` to 'Japan, China, Northern Mariana Islands'. As of foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-29/run.json the future is `status: OPEN`, listed in both `overdue` and `overdue_cold_start`, and still in `primary_iso3_dropped` (CHN) -- committed iso3 remains ['JPN'], unchanged since 2026-08-08. This is the only REAPPEARED event in the registry's history to date (checked against every futures[*].history entry). foreknown/resolutions/gdacs-tc-1001305.json already exists, written at the first closure: resolved_at '2026-08-25T06:04:45+00:00', verdict EPISODE_ENDED, with a reaction block covering exactly the three nights the future was open under the first episode (2026-08-22 to 2026-08-24, peak 12772 articles on 2026-08-23). obs-2026-08-27-1.json (PR #37) fixed verify.py so this coexistence -- a resolution on record while the same future is currently OPEN -- passes verification, on the correct reasoning that 'a resolution is a claim about the moment it was written, not a promise the future stays closed forever' (verify.py, lines 1276-1282). That fix makes the committed record internally consistent again, but it does not touch the other half of the same mechanism: practice/src/practice/foreknown/resolve.py's resolve_pending (lines 132-156) is documented as 'Idempotent and append-only: an existing resolution is never rewritten' and enforces this with `path = out_dir / f"{fid}.json"; if path.exists(): continue` (lines 145-147) -- keyed on future id alone, with no per-episode identity. When gdacs-tc-1001305 eventually closes a second time (a second CLOSED_BY_SOURCE or DISSIPATED history event), resolve_pending will see `future.get("status") != "OPEN"` (true), compute the same path, find it already exists, and `continue` -- skip it, permanently. No second resolution file will ever be written for this id. The reaction_series join that only happens inside resolve_future (resolve.py line 151-153, the only place a resolution's `reaction` block is populated) will never run for the 2026-08-28-onward episode. Every night this future spends OPEN in its second life -- already at least 2026-08-28 through 2026-08-29 and counting -- accrues attention and (if FTS lists a matching plan) money data in foreknown/reaction/ the same as any other OPEN future, but none of it will ever be joined into a resolution, because the file the join writes to is already taken by the first episode's numbers.
method: Scanned foreknown/registry.json's futures for every history entry with event == 'REAPPEARED' (python3 json load, one match: gdacs-tc-1001305, ts 2026-08-28T17:41:45+00:00) and cross-checked each against foreknown/resolutions/ for an existing file under the same id -- one match, foreknown/resolutions/gdacs-tc-1001305.json, resolved_at 2026-08-25T06:04:45+00:00, verdict EPISODE_ENDED. Compared that resolved_at against the future's own CLOSED_BY_SOURCE history event (same timestamp, confirming this is the fix obs-2026-08-27-1.json/PR #37 was written against) and against the current registry status (OPEN, per foreknown/registry.json and foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-29/run.json's overdue/overdue_cold_start/primary_iso3_dropped fields). Read practice/src/practice/foreknown/resolve.py end to end, in particular resolve_pending's file-existence guard (lines 145-147) and its own docstring's append-only claim (line 133), and traced that the `reaction` key is attached to a resolution dict only inside resolve_future's caller (lines 151-154), never anywhere else in the codebase -- confirmed by grep for `reaction_series` and for `resolution["reaction"]`/`resolution.get("reaction")` across practice/src/practice, one call site each. No live fetch; all evidence is committed registry, snapshot and resolution JSON plus the resolve.py source as it stands in this checkout.

figures.resolve_pending_guard: practice/src/practice/foreknown/resolve.py, lines 145-147: path.exists() -> continue, keyed on future id only

worth_watching_because: obs-2026-08-27-1.json's fix made verify.py stop treating a resolved-then-reappeared future as a hole, which was correct and necessary -- but 'the coexistence is valid' and 'the second episode gets measured' are different claims, and only the first is true today. This future's own committed history already shows the second episode is not a rounding artifact: two REVISED events, a window extension, and a still-standing iso3 divergence obs-2026-08-24-1.json and obs-2026-08-25-1.json already tracked in its first life. If it closes again, that whole second life -- however many nights, whatever attention or FTS-plan money moved during it -- goes into foreknown/reaction/ nightly the same as any OPEN future's does, but has no resolution file to be joined into, ever, because resolve_pending's guard is per-id, not per-episode. This is a clean, falsifiable prediction rather than an already-observed failure (the future is still OPEN; nothing has silently failed yet), and it will resolve itself the first time gdacs-tc-1001305 -- or any other future -- closes for a second time: either a discovery pass or the sentinel's own bookkeeping should then find foreknown/resolutions/ unchanged for that id despite a second CLOSED_BY_SOURCE/DISSIPATED event in its registry history, confirming the gap, or the maintainer decides resolutions should be keyed per-episode (e.g. `{fid}-{closed_at}.json`) before that happens, closing it. Filed as a new sensor, foreknown/proposals/sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json, since the check is purely mechanical (does a REAPPEARED-then-closed-again future have more than one resolution, or a resolution whose evidence extends past its own resolved_at) and needs no threshold, the same reasoning sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json's own definition gives for not needing one.
left_alone: Not changing resolve.py's guard or the resolutions/ file-naming scheme -- keying resolutions per-episode instead of per-future-id is a real design change to the registry's outcome-measurement layer (touching resolve_pending, the resolutions/ directory's own implicit schema, and everything downstream that reads foreknown/resolutions/*.json expecting one file per future id, including verify.py's own resolution-check loop), which is a decision for the maintainer, not something this observation's single not-yet-manifested instance settles. Not re-running the notary or fetching GDACS's live feed to see whether gdacs-tc-1001305 has closed again since 2026-08-29 -- that would be a fresh fetch outside what a difference observation cites (committed evidence only); the next sentinel run will notarize whatever the feed says on its own night, and either the prediction above holds or it doesn't. Not touching sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json's own review chain with a new entry tonight -- the CHN divergence surviving a full closure/reappearance cycle is consistent with, not a revision of, that sensor's 2026-08-24/2026-08-25 reviews (registry-side, permanent once closed), and this observation's own subject is the resolution layer, not the iso3 extraction layer; the two are related through the same future but are different mechanisms. Not writing a memoryhole/verdicts file -- memoryhole/readings/2026-08-28.json, the newest reading, carries zero rule-layer abstentions across all 20 entries. Not touching the other PROPOSED sensors: lead-time-pathway-idle now has 7 of the 10 FORECAST-kind resolutions its test_rule waits for (all seven NO_ALERT_MATCH, two forecasts -- nhc-ep112026, nhc-ep122026 -- still OPEN), short of the threshold; registry-stall and source-reconfirmation-blind-spot both carry open reviews asking for a firing-rule redesign, not more nights of the same data.
